# dj-hx

> Handler-first htmx 4 for Django. The view names the outcome with a verb (`render`, `page`, `fragment`,
> `invalid`, `redirect`, `navigate`, `removed`, `text`); the template keeps every request-side control; fragments are
> `{% partialdef %}` regions of the page template. Nothing depends on django-htmx. Every way htmx 4 fails
> silently is turned into a raised or recorded error with a message that says what to change.

Facts to hold while writing code against this package:

- Requires htmx **4** (`HX-Request-Type` header). htmx 1/2 idioms are rejected by a lint that runs on every
  test-client response. Django 4.2, 5.2, 6.0 and 6.1; Python 3.10 to 3.13.
- The only client fact a handler reads is `HX-Request-Type`: `full` (browser, boosted link, or a control
  whose target is `body` or that an `hx-select` reaches, its own or an ancestor's `hx-select:inherited`) or
  `partial` (a control targeting an element). Never
  read `HX-Source` or `HX-Target`; never branch on an element id.
- One template per resource. A fragment is a named `{% partialdef name inline %}` region of that page
  template. A partial name containing a dot (`rows.html`) is a separate file instead.
- Any partial delivered as an `<hx-partial>` (`.partial("count")`, the messages partial) must have exactly
  one root element whose `id` equals the partial's name.
- Verbs *raise* when the mistake is certain at call time. Everything else is *recorded* on
  `response.hx_findings`, logged to the `dj_hx` logger, and raised by `HxTestClient`. Production never 500s
  on a recorded finding.

## Install

Not on PyPI; install from the release tag:

```sh
pip install "dj-hx @ git+https://github.com/codetalcott/dj-hx@v0.1.0"
pip install "dj-hx[partials] @ git+https://github.com/codetalcott/dj-hx@v0.1.0"   # Django 4.2 to 5.x
```

```python
INSTALLED_APPS = [..., "django.contrib.messages", "dj_hx", ...]

MIDDLEWARE = [
    ...,
    "django.middleware.common.CommonMiddleware",
    "django.contrib.messages.middleware.MessageMiddleware",
    "dj_hx.middleware.HxMiddleware",          # AFTER MessageMiddleware (check dj_hx.E002)
]

HX_MESSAGES_TEMPLATE = "layout.html#messages"  # flash messages bridged into fragment responses
```

Django 4.2 to 5.x has no `{% partialdef %}`; install `django-template-partials` and register its tags
as a builtin (or every template must `{% load partials %}`). Django 6.0 needs none of this:

```python
import django
if django.VERSION < (6, 0):
    INSTALLED_APPS.insert(0, "template_partials")
    TEMPLATES[0]["OPTIONS"]["builtins"] = ["template_partials.templatetags.partials"]
```

Layout. In htmx 4 an attribute reaches descendants only with `:inherited`; a bare `hx-boost="true"` on
`<body>` boosts nothing. The CSRF header rides on every htmx request this way, including query-string
DELETEs. The messages partial is a `partialdef` so a fragment response can update it too.

```django
{% load static %}<!doctype html>
<html><head><script src="{% static 'js/htmx-4.0.0.js' %}"></script></head>
<body hx-boost:inherited="true" hx-headers:inherited='{"X-CSRFToken": "{{ csrf_token }}"}'>
{% partialdef messages inline %}
<div id="messages">{% for message in messages %}<div class="flash">{{ message }}</div>{% endfor %}</div>
{% endpartialdef %}
{% block content %}{% endblock %}
</body></html>
```

Template context processors must include `django.template.context_processors.request` and
`django.contrib.messages.context_processors.messages`.

## Choosing the verb

| The handler's outcome | Write |
|---|---|
| Same URL serves the page to a browser and one region to a control | `render(request, "index.html", "rows", ctx)` |
| Always the whole page (a detail or edit page) | `page(request, "show.html", ctx)` |
| Always a fragment: a polling widget, a region never served as a page | `fragment(request, "archive_ui.html", context=ctx)` or `fragment(request, "index.html", "rows", ctx)` |
| Form failed validation | `invalid(request, "new.html", "form", ctx)` (status 422; htmx 4 swaps it) |
| Success; the browser or a body-targeted control should land elsewhere | `redirect(request, "contacts", pk=3)` (plain 303) |
| Another page, whatever the control targets: a login check, an expired session | `navigate(request, "login")` (303, or `HX-Redirect` on a partial request) |
| Resource deleted; the control says `hx-swap="delete"` | `removed(request)` (200, empty body) |
| A short string into a span or an error slot | `text(request, "(3 total)")` (HTML-escaped) |
| One URL reached by both a body-targeted control and an element-targeted one | branch on `wants_page(request)` |

Never return `HttpResponse(status=204)`, `HttpResponseRedirect`, `django.shortcuts.redirect`,
`django.shortcuts.render` or `HttpResponse("")` to an htmx request. Say what happened with a verb: a
response no verb built that answers an element-targeted request is recorded as `HxBareResponse`.

Django's `login_required` answers with a 302, which the guard records when a control targets an element.
Leave the page instead; on a partial request `request.get_full_path()` is the fragment's URL, so come back
to the page, `current_url(request)`:

```python
from functools import wraps
from django.contrib.auth.views import redirect_to_login
from dj_hx import current_url, navigate

def hx_login_required(view):
    @wraps(view)
    def wrapper(request, *args, **kwargs):
        if request.user.is_authenticated:
            return view(request, *args, **kwargs)
        login = redirect_to_login(current_url(request) or request.get_full_path())
        return navigate(request, login["Location"])
    return wrapper
```

Messages added before `navigate` wait for the page it loads.

## API

Everything below is importable from `dj_hx`.

### Request side

```python
is_htmx(request) -> bool            # HX-Request: true
request_type(request) -> str|None   # "full" | "partial" | None (a browser)
wants_page(request) -> bool         # browser, boosted link, or body-targeted control
wants_fragment(request) -> bool     # a control targeting an element
current_url(request) -> str|None    # HX-Current-URL
vary_on_hx(response) -> response    # Vary: HX-Request, HX-Request-Type (the verbs and middleware do this)
```

An htmx request without `HX-Request-Type` raises `HxProtocolError` (this needs htmx 4). A proxy that strips
the header can be worked around with `HX_REQUEST_TYPE_FALLBACK = "full"` or `"partial"`; the guard still
records the finding.

### Verbs

```python
render(request, template, partial, context=None, *, status=200) -> HxResponse
    # wants_page: the page. Otherwise: the partial of `template` (or the file if `partial` has a dot).

page(request, template, context=None) -> HxResponse
    # Always the page. RAISES HxPageIntoFragment on a partial request.

fragment(request, template, partial=None, context=None) -> HxResponse
    # Always a fragment: the file `template`, or `partial` of it. RECORDS HxFragmentIntoPage
    # when a boosted or body-targeted htmx request would put a bare fragment into <body>.

invalid(request, template, partial, context=None) -> HxResponse
    # render() with status 422. No client configuration needed; htmx 4 swaps 422 bodies.

redirect(request, to, *args, code=303, **kwargs) -> HxRedirectResponse
    # `to` resolves like django.shortcuts.redirect (URL name, model, or URL).
    # RAISES HxRedirectIntoFragment on a partial request (fetch would follow it into the element).

navigate(request, to, *args, **kwargs) -> HxRedirectResponse | HxResponse
    # `to` resolves like redirect(). Leave the page whatever the control targets: a plain 303 when the
    # request wants a page; on a partial request a 200 with an empty body and HX-Redirect, a full page load.

removed(request) -> HxResponse
    # 200 with an empty body. The control's hx-swap="delete" removes its own representation.

text(request, value) -> HxResponse
    # str(value), HTML-escaped. RECORDS HxFragmentIntoPage on a full htmx request.
```

Every verb sets `Vary`. Under `DEBUG` the response carries `X-HX-Template: index.html#rows`.

### Response methods

`HxResponse` (an `HttpResponse`) and `HxRedirectResponse` (a 303) share these; all return `self`:

```python
.trigger(name, *, target="body", **detail)   # HX-Trigger, always JSON, always with a target
.partial(name, template=None)                # append <hx-partial hx-target="#name" hx-swap="outerHTML">
                                             # rendered from the page template with the same context;
                                             # only on fragment responses (no-op on a page); root id checked
.push_url(url) / .replace_url(url)           # HX-Push-Url / HX-Replace-Url
.with_status(code)
.retarget(selector) / .reswap(spec)          # escape hatches: the template can no longer predict the
                                             # DOM effect. Use with a comment saying why.
```

`.trigger()` always sets a `target` because after a `delete` swap the requesting element is gone and htmx 4
would dispatch on `document`, where an `hx-trigger="x from:body"` listener cannot hear it. `detail` keys are
unpacked into the scope of `hx-on` handlers.

```python
return render(request, "index.html", "rows", ctx).trigger("contacts-changed")
return fragment(request, "index.html", "rows", ctx).partial("count")   # also refreshes #count
```

### Generic views

```python
from dj_hx import HxMixin

class ContactList(HxMixin, ListView):          # HxMixin FIRST (check dj_hx.E007)
    model = Contact
    template_name = "index.html"
    partial = "rows"                            # None means page() only, which raises on a partial request

class ContactCreate(HxMixin, CreateView):
    model = Contact
    fields = ["first", "last", "email"]
    template_name = "new.html"
    partial = "form"
    success_url = reverse_lazy("contacts")
```

`HxMixin` overrides three hooks: `render_to_response` (goes through `render` when `partial` is set, else
`page`), `form_invalid` (422), and `form_valid` (raises `HxRedirectIntoFragment` if Django's redirect would
answer a partial request; override it to return `render`/`fragment`/`removed` for element-targeted forms).

### Interactions

One handler bound to one partial. The reply is always that partial.

```python
from dj_hx import interaction

def assign_context(request, contest):     # the page view calls it too: every name the page reads has its default here
    return {"contest": Contest.get(contest), "notified": False, "error": None}

@interaction("POST", partial="contests/assign.html#notify", context=assign_context,
             refuses=(DomainError,), triggers=("notified",), route=None)
def notify(request, contest: str, member: int):
    Contest.get(contest).notify(member)
    return {"notified": True}             # a dict of context keys, or None; never a response
```

```python
urlpatterns = [..., path("", include("dj_hx.urls"))]   # once, at the site root
```

```django
{% load hx %}
<button hx-post="{% act 'notify' contest=contest.slug member=member.id %}" hx-target="#notify" hx-swap="outerHTML">
```

- Route: `x/<app label>/<handler>/<param>/.../`, `<int:p>` for a parameter annotated `int` and `<str:p>`
  otherwise, named after the handler in the `dj_hx` namespace. `route="reviewers/<int:member>/notify"` sets
  the path instead and must name exactly the handler's parameters, `<int:...>` for each `int` one.
- `{% act %}` takes keyword arguments only, one per handler parameter. A positional argument, an unknown or
  a missing keyword, or an unknown interaction raises `TemplateSyntaxError` at render. Without `dj_hx.urls`
  included it raises `ImproperlyConfigured`, naming `path("", include("dj_hx.urls"))`.
- Put interactions in an installed app's `views.py`: dj-hx's `ready()` imports the `views` module of every
  app outside site-packages. One registered after `dj_hx.urls` was first read keeps the bare view as its
  route, without the decorators above it (check E017).
- Django view decorators go ABOVE `@interaction` (`@login_required` then `@interaction(...)`). It returns the
  routed view and `dj_hx.urls` routes whatever the module that defines the handler holds under the handler's
  name, as written, so every decorator above it wraps the route, a hand-written one included. Write your own
  with `functools.wraps`, so dj-hx's messages and `hx_map` name the handler (W018 warns on one without it).
  Below it, a decorator that returns a response is a return-type error (W019 warns on any decorator below).
  The module must hold the view `@interaction` returned (or a decorator of it) under the handler's name, never
  the raw handler: `remind_view = interaction(...)(remind)` raises when the URLconf is read; write
  `remind = interaction(...)(remind)` in the module that defines `remind` (the handler is
  `inspect.unwrap(remind)`). An interaction the module does not hold under its name gets the bare view, and
  decorators applied to it are dropped. `login_required`'s 302 to a control that targets an element is
  recorded by the guard (`HxRedirectIntoFragment`), as for any view.
- Reply: `fragment()` of the partial with `context(request, <the route parameters it names>)` and the
  returned keys over it, status 200, then `.trigger(name)` for each of `triggers`. A `context=` parameter the
  route lacks takes its default. Its root element must carry `id="<partial name>"` (`HxPartialRootId`).
- Every reply carries `error`: `str(exc)` on a refusal, `None` on success unless `context=` or the handler sets
  it, so the partial reads `{% if error %}` whatever `context=` defines. The page view is not a reply: a page
  that renders the partial needs `error` in its own context (as `assign_context` has it), or `HxTestClient`
  raises `HxUndefinedVariable` on the page.
- Refusal: an exception in `refuses` (one class, or a tuple of them) re-renders the partial with
  `error=str(exc)`, status 422, no triggers. Any other exception is a 500. Any other method is a 405.
  Give every refusal a message the user can read: an empty or blank one is recorded as `HxEmptyRefusal`
  (the reply still goes out, showing nothing), which `HxTestClient` raises.
- A refusal is a response, so under `ATOMIC_REQUESTS` the writes made before the raise are COMMITTED. Raise
  before writing, or call `transaction.set_rollback(True)` just before the raise, or write inside
  `with transaction.atomic():` and raise inside it (that works without `ATOMIC_REQUESTS` too).
- Access control: a decorator above `@interaction`, or middleware that sees every request (Django 5.1's
  `LoginRequiredMiddleware`). Interactions are routed by the root `include("dj_hx.urls")`, so protection on
  the app's own include (`decorator_include`, a middleware matching the app's URL prefix) never reaches them.
- `ImproperlyConfigured` when the URLconf is first read (first request, `manage.py check`): the module holds
  the raw handler under its name, or a decorator of it written with `functools.wraps`. One written without
  `functools.wraps` is routed as it is, past the method guard; only W018 warns.
- `ImproperlyConfigured` at import: a duplicate name, a minted route for a handler in no installed app, a
  `route=` that does not match, `partial=` not `page.html#name`, `triggers=` a string, `method` not one of
  GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE (any case), `refuses` holding anything but exception classes, `*args` or
  `**kwargs` on the handler or on `context=`, a `context=` parameter without a default that the route lacks.
  At the reply: a return that is not a dict or `None` (a view decorator below `@interaction` returning a
  response included), or a returned key the context lacks (`error` never is: every reply carries it).
- `manage.py check` reads each `{% act %}` in the project's `.html`/`.htm` templates (never site-packages; one
  inside `{% verbatim %}` still counts, for E009 and as E014's control) and the control
  whose verb attribute holds it, resolving each attribute as htmx 4.0.2 does. The verb must send the
  interaction's method (`hx-action` sends its `hx-method`, an ancestor's `hx-method:inherited`, its
  `method` attribute, else GET; a submit button's `formmethod` is not read). The control must target the
  element with the partial's id: `hx-target="#<partial>"` (or an htmx 4.0.2 extended selector whose CSS
  part is that: `closest`, `find`, `findAll`, `next`, `previous`, optionally after `global `), or no
  `hx-target` / `hx-target="this"` on the element carrying the id (`this` is the element that declares it). `hx-swap` must be an outer swap
  (`outerHTML`, `outerMorph` or `outerSync`; each measured to leave one element with the id on htmx 4.0.2).
  Each attribute is the control's own or an ancestor's
  `:inherited` one; a plain attribute on an ancestor does not count. A computed `hx-swap` or `hx-method` is
  not judged; a templated id or `hx-target` is judged by its literal parts and skipped only when it could
  equal the expected value (`id="{{ name }}"` is skipped, `id="row-{{ pk }}"` is an Error). A block tag in
  an id, and the text it wraps, counts as computed (`id="{% if p %}{{ p }}-{% endif %}notify"` is skipped). An `{% act %}`
  outside a verb attribute gets Info I021. The ids are in the checks table below.

Status policy for a site with interactions (measured on htmx 4.0.2 and _hyperscript 0.9.94 in Chromium,
`tests/test_interactions_browser.py`). Without it a 404, 405 or 500 swaps its body over the region and the
controls are gone. The pair goes on the root element of each interaction's partial, the alert once in the
layout:

```django
<div id="notify" hx-status:40x:inherited="swap:none" hx-status:5xx:inherited="swap:none">   {# "40x" is 400-409, so 422 still swaps #}
<p id="trouble" role="alert" style="display: none"
   _="on htmx:before:request from body hide me end
      on htmx:error from body show me end
      on htmx:response:error from body if event.detail.ctx.response.status is not 422 show me">Something went wrong. Please try again.</p>
```

- The `:inherited` pair reaches every control inside the partial, and each reply carries it back. A control
  outside the partial that targets it writes the pair itself: `hx-status:40x="swap:none" hx-status:5xx="swap:none"`.
- NOT `htmx-config`'s `noSwap: [204, 304, "40x", "5xx"]`: htmx 4.0.2 applies it to every htmx request on the
  page, boosted links and forms included, and checks it before any `hx-status`, so nothing can opt back in. A
  boosted link to a page that answers 404 then keeps the old page under the new URL (measured); under the
  scoped pair it shows the 404 page.
- One generic alert in the layout. `htmx:response:error` fires for every status >= 400, 422 included, so it
  skips 422 (the partial shows the refusal). A request with no reply (server down, a network error, a
  timeout) or a swap that throws fires `htmx:error` instead, so it hears that too. It hides itself when the
  next request starts.
- Hide it with `style="display: none"`, NEVER the `hidden` attribute: hyperscript's `show` clears only an
  inline `display`, so a `hidden` alert never appears.
- Hear a `triggers=` fact with `_="on notified from body ..."` or `hx-trigger="notified from:body"`. It runs
  after the reply; feedback belongs in the reply or a listener, never in an `on click` that runs before it.

### Settings

| Setting | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `HX_MESSAGES_TEMPLATE = "layout.html#messages"` | Partial used to render pending `django.contrib.messages` into fragment responses. `#name` defaults to `messages`. Root element must be `id="<name>"`. |
| `HX_REQUEST_TYPE_FALLBACK = "full"` | Answer htmx requests missing `HX-Request-Type` as this type instead of raising. Proxies only. |
| `HX_LINT_IGNORE = ("implicit-inheritance",)` | Lint rules to silence everywhere (test client, middleware, `hx_lint`, W005). |
| `HX_EXTENSIONS = ("hx-live", "sse")` | Extensions the pages load, for the lint (also detected from `<script src>`). The file name (`hx-sse`) or the name htmx registers (`sse`, as in `htmx.config.extensions`); W008 flags any other. |
| `SILENCED_SYSTEM_CHECKS = ["dj_hx.W005"]` | Standard Django; the check ids are below. An Error's id can be silenced too, as while working through E022's first run on an existing site: an Error stops `check`, `runserver`, `migrate`, `makemigrations`, `createsuperuser` and `manage.py test`. |

### Errors

All subclass `HxError` except `HxRedirectError` (an `AssertionError` from the test client).

| Error | Raised or recorded | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| `HxPageIntoFragment` | raised by `page()` | page answers an element-targeted request | `hx-target="body"` on the control, or `render(..., partial)` |
| `HxRedirectIntoFragment` | raised by `redirect()` / `HxMixin.form_valid`; recorded by the guard for any other 3xx, including `APPEND_SLASH`'s 301 | 3xx answers an element-targeted request | target body, `navigate()` to leave the page, or return a fragment; match the route's trailing slash (`{% url %}` does) |
| `HxFragmentIntoPage` | recorded by `fragment()` / `text()` | bare fragment answers a boosted or body-targeted request | target an element, or render a page |
| `HxNoSwap` | recorded by the guard | 204 answers a partial request; htmx 4 does not swap | `removed()` + `hx-swap="delete"`, or a fragment |
| `HxBareResponse` | recorded by the guard | a `text/html` 2xx no verb built answers an element-targeted request (`django.shortcuts.render`, `HttpResponse`, `TemplateResponse`) | use a verb, or `HxMixin` on a generic view |
| `HxMessagesUnconfigured` | recorded by the middleware | messages added on a fragment response, `HX_MESSAGES_TEMPLATE` unset | set it |
| `HxProtocolError` | raised by `request_type()`; recorded by the guard | `HX-Request` without `HX-Request-Type` | use htmx 4; `HX_REQUEST_TYPE_FALLBACK` for proxies |
| `HxUnknownPartial` | raised at render | `partial=` names no partial of the template; message lists the ones it defines | write `{% partialdef name inline %}` around the region |
| `HxEmptyRefusal` | recorded by an interaction's reply | a declared refusal with an empty or blank message: the 422 reply's `{% if error %}` shows nothing | raise it with a message: `raise NotOnRota("Member 9 is not on the rota.")` |
| `HxPartialRootId` | raised at render | a partial used as `<hx-partial>`, or an interaction's reply, does not start with one element carrying `id="<name>"` | wrap the region in `<div id="name">` |
| `HxLintError` | raised by `HxTestClient` | an error-level lint finding in a `text/html` response | fix the HTML; `lint_ignore=` / `HX_LINT_IGNORE` to silence a rule |
| `HxRedirectError` | raised by `HxTestClient` | 3xx to a `full=True` request without `follow=` | pass `follow=True` (what the browser shows) or `follow=False` (assert on the 3xx) |
| `HxUndefinedVariable` | raised by `HxTestClient`; recorded under `strict=False` | a project template reads a name nobody supplies or an attribute an object lacks, in `{{ }}`, `{% if %}`, `{% for %}` or any tag (lookups that depend on the data are skipped: see Testing); `.lookups` names each with its template:line | put the name in the view's context with its default (an interaction's: `context=`), or correct it; `undefined=False` turns the check off |

## Templates

A page defines its fragments inline. `inline` renders the region in place on the page; the handler
names it to render it alone.

```django
{% extends "layout.html" %}
{% block content %}
<table><tbody>
{% partialdef rows inline %}
{% for contact in contacts %}
<tr>
  <td>{{ contact.first }}</td>
  <td><a href="#" hx-delete="{% url 'contacts_view' contact.id %}"
                  hx-confirm="Delete?" hx-target="closest tr" hx-swap="delete swap:1s">Delete</a></td>
</tr>
{% endfor %}
{% endpartialdef %}
</tbody></table>

{% partialdef count inline %}<span id="count">{{ contacts|length }}</span>{% endpartialdef %}

<span id="total" hx-get="{% url 'contacts_count' %}" hx-trigger="revealed, contacts-changed from:body"></span>
{% endblock %}
```

A form region for `invalid()`:

```django
{% partialdef form inline %}
<form id="form" action="{% url 'contacts_new' %}" method="post">
  {% csrf_token %}
  <input name="email" value="{{ contact.email }}"
         hx-get="{% url 'contacts_email' contact.id %}" hx-target="next .error"
         hx-trigger="change, keyup delay:200ms changed">
  <span class="error">{{ contact.errors.email }}</span>
  <button>Save</button>
</form>
{% endpartialdef %}
```

A button whose response is a page (a redirect after delete from an edit page):

```django
<button hx-delete="{% url 'contacts_view' contact.id %}" hx-target="body" hx-push-url="true">Delete</button>
```

htmx 4 rules the templates rely on (verified against htmx.js 4.0.0):

- `HX-Request-Type` is `full` when the target is `body`, an `hx-select` reaches the element (its own or an
  ancestor's `hx-select:inherited`; an own `hx-select=""` is no select), or the element is boosted. The reply
  is cut down to what that selector finds in it before the swap.
- Attributes reach descendants only with `:inherited` (`hx-target:inherited`, `hx-boost:inherited`).
- `hx-delete` sends its parameters in the query string and excludes the enclosing form unless
  `hx-include="closest form"`; the handler reads them from `request.GET`.
- A `delete` swap runs regardless of response content and honors `swap:1s`.
- Only 204 and 304 skip the swap. A 422 body swaps, and so do a 404, a 405 and a 5xx (wiping the region an
  interaction's control sits in), unless the partial's root sets the status policy (under Interactions).
- `hx-push-url="true"` pushes the URL after a redirect, so a plain 303 updates the location bar.
- An `HX-Redirect` response header makes htmx load that URL as a full page and skip the swap.
- Events are colon-separated (`hx-on::after:swap`, `htmx:after:swap`); modifiers are `from:body`,
  `delay:200ms`, `changed`, `once`, `throttle:1s`; swap styles are case-sensitive (`outerHTML`).

## htmx 2 is rejected

Agents default to htmx 1/2. These are what the lint reports (`[error]` raises in tests):

| Do not write | Write | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| `hx-ext="..."` | nothing; loading the extension script is enough | `htmx2-attribute` |
| `hx-vars`, `hx-params`, `hx-disinherit`, `hx-inherit`, `hx-request`, `hx-history`, `hx-disabled-elt` | `hx-vals='js:...'`, `htmx:config:request`, `:inherited`, `hx-config`, `hx-disable` | `htmx2-attribute` |
| `<body hx-boost="true">` (even when the links are in child templates) | `<body hx-boost:inherited="true">` | `boost-not-inherited` |
| `<div hx-target="#x">` over children | `hx-target:inherited="#x"` | `implicit-inheritance` (warning) |
| `hx-on::afterSwap`, `hx-on::after-request`, `hx-trigger="htmx:afterSwap from:body"`, `htmx:configRequest` | `hx-on::after:swap`, `hx-on::after:request`, `hx-trigger="htmx:after:swap from:body"`, `htmx:config:request` | `htmx2-event-name` |
| `hx-swap="outerhtml"` | `hx-swap="outerHTML"` | `swap-style-case` |
| `hx-swap="innerHTML show:#x:top"` | `hx-swap="innerHTML show:top showTarget:#x"` | `swap-show-syntax` |
| `hx-trigger="click queue:all"` | `hx-sync="this:queue all"` | `trigger-queue` |
| `hx-trigger="click from:closest form"` | `hx-trigger="click from:'closest form'"` | `trigger-unquoted-selector` |
| `hx-delete` with the default swap on `closest tr` | `hx-swap="delete"` or `outerHTML` | `delete-default-swap` (warning) |
| `hx-target="#nope"` with no such id on the page | an existing id | `missing-target` |
| two elements with the same literal `id` (an id built with `{{ }}` is not compared; one in two exclusive `{% if %}` branches is reported) | unique ids | `duplicate-id` |
| `hx-select="#main"` with a non-body target | let the server send the fragment | `select-not-body` (info) |

Also `unknown-attribute`, `unknown-swap-style`, `unknown-swap-modifier`, `unknown-trigger-modifier`,
`trigger-syntax`, `extension-not-loaded` (warning), `delete-without-include` (info). Each message suggests
the nearest valid name.

## Testing

```python
from dj_hx.testing import HxTestClient, assert_no_hx_check_issues

client = HxTestClient()                       # strict=True, lint=True, lint_ignore=(), undefined=True
client.get("/contacts/")                      # a browser
client.hx_get("/contacts/?q=a")               # HX-Request: true, HX-Request-Type: partial
client.hx_get("/contacts/", full=True)        # a boosted link or body-targeted control
client.hx_post("/contacts/new/", {"email": "x"})            # partial: expect 422 or a fragment
client.hx_post("/contacts/new/", form, full=True, follow=True)   # what the browser shows after the 303
client.hx_delete("/contacts/3/", full=True, follow=False)   # assert on the 303 itself
client.hx_delete("/contacts/?selected_contact_ids=1")       # DELETE params go in the query string
client.hx_put("/x/", {"a": 1})                # form-encoded; json={...} sends application/json

def test_dj_hx_is_configured():
    assert_no_hx_check_issues()               # pytest never runs system checks; this does
```

`assert_no_hx_check_issues()` fails on any dj-hx check message, Infos (I021, I023) included;
`include_warnings=False` keeps Errors only.

What the client enforces on every request, including plain `client.get`:

- Recorded findings (the verbs' and the guard's) raise the first one, with every other finding on that response listed in its message. `HxTestClient(strict=False)` records
  instead.
- Every `text/html` response is linted; an error-level finding raises `HxLintError`, a warning is a
  `HxLintWarning` (`warnings.warn`). `lint=False` or `lint_ignore=("rule",)` per client.
- A 3xx to a `full=True` request raises `HxRedirectError` unless `follow=True` or `follow=False` was
  chosen, because htmx's fetch follows redirects and the browser never sees the 3xx.
- A project template that reads a name nobody supplies, or an attribute an object lacks, raises
  `HxUndefinedVariable`, a recorded finding (`strict=False` leaves it in `response.hx_findings`). Its
  `.lookups` give each one's `variable` (the name, or the attribute after a dot), `template`, `line`, `tag`
  and `included`, where the tag is written: an `{% extends %}` base, an included file, the file a partial is in.
  - Raises: `{{ x }}`, `{% if x %}`, `{% for i in x %}` and `{{ x|default:"" }}` (Django logs the lookup before
    any filter runs) for a name nobody supplies, an `{% include %}` parameter not passed (the message says to
    pass it in the include's `with`, `... subtitle=None`), and `{{ obj.attr }}` for an attribute a non-None
    object lacks that is not a mapping key or an index (`{{ user.emial }}`, `{{ items.length }}` on a list).
  - Skipped, because the outcome depends on the data: a lookup on None (`obj.rel.name` with no `rel`), a key
    a `Mapping` or the session lacks (`request.GET.stage`, `request.session.cart`; so a misspelt dict key is
    silent, as in Django, and so is any lookup on a mapping: `forloop.countr`, since `forloop` is a dict, and a
    misspelt QueryDict method, `request.GET.urlencod`), an index past the end of a sequence (`items.0` on `[]`; a string's index still
    counts), anything `{% firstof %}` reads, `debug` and `sql_queries` where the debug context processor is
    configured, and a response built from an exception (the 500 page).
  - Not seen: templates in site-packages or built from a string, a lookup that raised an exception Django
    silences (`DoesNotExist`), a render outside the request's context (a `ThreadPoolExecutor`, a plain thread,
    a streaming body consumed after the request). An `async def` view is checked.
  - It rests on Django details the suite pins on 4.2 to 6.1: the DEBUG record's message and its
    `VariableDoesNotExist`, the template node on the stack, and the exception's `params == (bit, current)`. A
    Django that changed the record or the node would make it go quiet; one that dropped `params` would make it
    count the lookups it now skips.
  - Supply each name from the view's context with its default. Read from Django's `django.template` DEBUG
    log while the request runs; other handlers see only what they saw before. `undefined=False` turns it off.
    `logging.disable()` in force, or a disabled `django.template` logger (a `LOGGING` dict leaving
    `disable_existing_loggers` at `True`), raises `ImproperlyConfigured`, because the check would see nothing.
- Without `HxMiddleware` installed the client runs the guard itself.

Assertions that match the protocol:

```python
r = client.hx_delete("/contacts/3/")                       # a row's link, hx-swap="delete"
assert r.status_code == 200 and b"<tr>" not in r.content
assert r.content.decode().startswith('\n<hx-partial hx-target="#messages" hx-swap="outerHTML">')

r = client.hx_delete("/contacts/?selected_contact_ids=1&selected_contact_ids=2")
assert json.loads(r["HX-Trigger"]) == {"contacts-changed": {"target": "body"}}

with pytest.raises(HxPageIntoFragment, match=r"contacts_view\(\) renders the page"):
    client.hx_get("/contacts/3/")                          # a page-only view reached by a partial control
```

## Tools and checks

```
manage.py hx_lint [paths...] [--warnings-as-errors]   # htmx 4 lint over template source, never site-packages
manage.py hx_map [--no-check] [--by-template]          # controls <-> views <-> events, checked
```

`--by-template` inverts the map: every template and partial a view names, who renders it, and the
controls that reach them.

Site-packages, wherever dj-hx skips it (`hx_lint`, `hx_map`, the checks, `ready()`), is sysconfig's
`purelib` and `platlib` plus the `site-packages` and `dist-packages` directories `site` reports, the user
one (`pip install --user`) included.

`hx_map` classifies each control as full or partial by htmx 4's rule, resolves it through `{% url %}`,
`{% act %}` (the interaction registry: an interaction answers its one method with its partial through
`fragment()` and announces its `triggers=`; an `{% act %}` naming no interaction, or with `dj_hx.urls` not
included, is an error) or the literal path, and errors when a partial control reaches a view that only calls `page`, or a full
control reaches one that only calls `fragment`/`text`/`removed`; `navigate` says nothing about shape, so a
view that calls it and `page` is still page-only. `if request.method == "DELETE":` branches
are attributed to that method. It pairs `.trigger("x")` with `hx-trigger="x from:body"` or a hyperscript `_="on x from body ..."` (or the same in an inline `<script type="text/hyperscript">`, behaviors included) both ways (a listener for a browser event such as `click`, a hyperscript observer (`on intersection`, `on mutation`, `on resize`), or a name with a colon (`htmx:*`, an extension's `sse:message`, a namespaced `contact:saved`) is never asked to be announced and still pairs; one built in the template is not read as a listener; an event a script names, `addEventListener('x', ...)` or a hyperscript `send x`, counts for both sides; checks W024 and W025 report the same pairing) and warns
on `hx-delete` controls that send no values to a handler that reads them. Whether or not a view calls a
verb, it errors when the view reads the `HX-Trigger` request header (`request.headers`, `request.META`),
which htmx 4 does not send, or reads `request.POST` on DELETE, which htmx 4 sends as query parameters
(`request.GET`); it warns when a view reads `HX-Target` or `HX-Source`.

System checks (tag `dj_hx`):

| ID | Fires when |
|---|---|
| W001 | `HxMiddleware` not installed |
| E002 | `HxMiddleware` listed before `MessageMiddleware` |
| W003 | `django.contrib.messages` installed but `HX_MESSAGES_TEMPLATE` unset |
| W004 | `HX_MESSAGES_TEMPLATE` does not resolve to a template partial |
| W005 | a project template fails the lint |
| W006 | Django < 6 without django-template-partials |
| E007 | a Django base class listed before `HxMixin` shadows its hooks |
| W008 | `HX_EXTENSIONS` is a string, or names an extension htmx 4 does not ship |
| E009 | `{% act %}` in a project template names no interaction (lists those there are) |
| E010 | `{% act %}`'s arguments are not its handler's parameters (positional, unknown or missing) |
| E011 | an `{% act %}` control's verb (`hx-get` ... `hx-delete`; or `hx-action` with its `hx-method`, an ancestor's `hx-method:inherited`, its `method` attribute, else GET; `formmethod` not read) is not the interaction's method |
| E012 | an `{% act %}` control does not target the element with id `<partial>`: neither `hx-target="#<partial>"` (own or an ancestor's `:inherited`; also `closest`, `find`, `findAll`, `next` or `previous #<partial>`, with or without `global `, as htmx 4.0.2's target resolver reads them) nor no `hx-target` / `hx-target="this"` on that element. A comma list, bare `next`/`previous`, `document`, `window`, `body`, `host` and other CSS are Errors |
| E013 | an `{% act %}` control's `hx-swap` (own or `:inherited`) is not an outer swap (`outerHTML`, `outerMorph`, `outerSync`, per htmx 4.0.2's swap code). A control without `hx-swap` is judged as htmx 4's default `innerHTML`; a page's `htmx.config.defaultSwap` is not read (write `hx-swap` on each control). Measured on htmx 4.0.2: htmx 4's default `innerHTML`, and `beforeend`, `afterbegin`, `beforebegin`, `afterend`, leave a second element with the id; on `innerMorph` htmx throws (`HierarchyRequestError`, logged as `htmx:error`) and the reply never reaches the page |
| E014 | an interaction has no control: no project `.html`/`.htm` template writes its `{% act %}` (a `{% url 'dj_hx:…' %}` or hand-written path is not counted: E011-E013 cannot check it); skipped for a handler whose module is in site-packages, whose templates are never read |
| E015 | an interaction's partial does not load (`HxUnknownPartial`'s reason) or does not parse (Django's `TemplateSyntaxError` message) |
| E016 | an interaction's partial does not start with an element carrying `id="<partial>"`, where the source shows its root |
| E017 | `dj_hx.urls` routes an interaction to other than what its module holds: it was registered after `dj_hx.urls` was first read, or the module rebound the name since |
| W018 | the module attribute routed for an interaction does not unwrap to it (a decorator above without `functools.wraps`) |
| W019 | a decorator sits below `@interaction` (the handler has `__wrapped__`) |
| E020 | interactions are registered but `dj_hx.urls` is not included |
| I021 | an `{% act %}` the checks cannot tie to one element's verb attribute (script, text, another attribute, `as`, a variable name) |
| E022 | a `{% url %}` with a quoted name in a project `.html`/`.htm` template does not reverse, against `ROOT_URLCONF`, with the arguments it passes: no such name (close ones listed), a namespace no URLconf installs, the wrong positional count or keywords, or both kinds mixed. Each argument is reversed with a placeholder for its route's converter (`int` 1; `str`, `slug`, `path` "a"; `uuid` all zeros); a keyword naming a route's extra kwarg gets that default. Skipped: `{% url ... as var %}` (Django's form for a view that may be missing), a name built at run time (a variable, a filter), a tag in a comment or `{% verbatim %}`. A site that sets `request.urlconf` per request silences it. The result depends on the settings it runs under: a route included only under `DEBUG` or a feature flag is an E022 under other settings (a deploy's `migrate` runs the checks); link it as `{% url 'name' as link %}{% if link %}...{% endif %}` |
| I023 | a `{% url %}` not checked: its route takes a custom converter or a `re_path` group, which has no placeholder. Usually a third-party `re_path` in a template the project overrides: admin's `{% url 'admin:app_list' app_label=... %}`, allauth's `account_confirm_email` |
| W024 | an event a view announces with `.trigger()` (as `hx_map` finds it) or an interaction declares in `triggers=` that no project template listens for (`hx-trigger`, `hx-on`, hyperscript `on` in `_`/`script`/`data-script` or an inline `<script type="text/hyperscript">`, behaviors included); an interaction in site-packages is not warned about |
| W025 | an event a project template listens for that nothing announces; browser events, hyperscript's observers (`on intersection`, `on mutation`, `on resize`) and names with a colon (`htmx:*`, `sse:message`, `contact:saved`) are left out, though they still pair with a `.trigger()` or `triggers=` of that name (so no W024); a name built in the template is not read as a listener. For both, an event a script in the templates names (a quoted name in a `<script>` or `hx-on`, a hyperscript `send`/`trigger`, even inside a quoted string) counts as heard and announced. W024 and W025 are Warnings because a JavaScript file, a hyperscript file (`<script type="text/hyperscript" src=...>`), an Alpine listener (`@x.window`, `x-on:`; not read), a template in site-packages or a helper the view calls can be the other side; both skip without `ROOT_URLCONF` |
| E026 | an `hx-select` reaches an `{% act %}` control: its own, or the nearest ancestor's `hx-select:inherited` (htmx 4 has no `hx-disinherit`; an own `hx-select=""` is an empty value, no select, and stops an ancestor's). htmx 4 then sends `HX-Request-Type: full`, so each reply records `HxFragmentIntoPage`, and swaps in only what the selector finds in the reply. Measured on htmx 4.0.2: a selector that matches nothing in the reply removes the partial's region; one that matches inside it puts that element in the region's place. A computed `hx-select` is not judged |

`HxMiddleware` also: adds `Vary` to every response, runs the guard, bridges pending messages onto partial
2xx HTML responses (peeking before consuming), logs findings as warnings on the `dj_hx` logger, and under
`DEBUG` lints every htmx response (`X-HX-Template` is set by the verb that rendered the response).

## A resource end to end

Function views, abridged from the example app (*Hypermedia Systems*' contact.app on the ORM):

```python
from django.contrib import messages
from django.views.decorators.http import require_http_methods
from dj_hx import invalid, page, redirect, removed, render, text, wants_page

@require_http_methods(["GET", "DELETE"])
def contacts(request):
    if request.method == "DELETE":                       # bulk delete: hx-include="closest form"
        for contact_id in request.GET.getlist("selected_contact_ids"):
            Contact.find(contact_id).delete()
        messages.success(request, "Deleted Contacts!")
        return render(request, "index.html", "rows", {"contacts": Contact.all(1)}).trigger("contacts-changed")
    q = request.GET.get("q")
    contacts_set = Contact.search(q) if q is not None else Contact.all(int(request.GET.get("page", 1)))
    return render(request, "index.html", "rows", {"contacts": contacts_set})

def contacts_count(request):
    return text(request, f"({Contact.count()} total Contacts)")

@require_http_methods(["GET", "POST"])
def contacts_new(request):
    if request.method == "GET":
        return page(request, "new.html", {"contact": Contact()})
    c = Contact(first=request.POST["first_name"], last=request.POST["last_name"], email=request.POST["email"])
    if not c.validate():
        return invalid(request, "new.html", "form", {"contact": c})
    c.save()
    messages.success(request, "Created New Contact!")
    return redirect(request, "contacts")

@require_http_methods(["GET", "DELETE"])
def contacts_view(request, contact_id):
    contact = Contact.find(contact_id)
    if request.method == "DELETE":
        contact.delete()
        messages.success(request, "Deleted Contact!")
        if wants_page(request):          # the edit page's button targets the body
            return redirect(request, "contacts")
        return removed(request)          # a row's link says hx-swap="delete"
    return page(request, "show.html", {"contact": contact})

def contacts_email(request, contact_id):   # inline validation into <span class="error">
    c = Contact.find(contact_id)
    c.email = request.GET.get("email", "")
    c.validate()
    return text(request, c.errors.get("email", ""))
```

```python
urlpatterns = [
    path("contacts/", views.contacts, name="contacts"),
    path("contacts/count/", views.contacts_count, name="contacts_count"),
    path("contacts/new/", views.contacts_new, name="contacts_new"),
    path("contacts/<int:contact_id>/", views.contacts_view, name="contacts_view"),
    path("contacts/<int:contact_id>/email/", views.contacts_email, name="contacts_email"),
]
```

Trailing slashes matter: a control whose URL misses one gets `APPEND_SLASH`'s 301, which the guard reports
as `HxRedirectIntoFragment`. Always build URLs with `{% url %}`, or `{% act %}` for an interaction.

- [README.md](https://github.com/codetalcott/dj-hx/blob/main/README.md): the design, the vocabulary, the silent-failure catalogue
- [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/codetalcott/dj-hx/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md): release notes
- [dj_hx/verbs.py](https://github.com/codetalcott/dj-hx/blob/main/dj_hx/verbs.py): the verbs and `HxResponse`
- [dj_hx/request.py](https://github.com/codetalcott/dj-hx/blob/main/dj_hx/request.py): `HX-Request-Type` and the `wants_*` helpers
- [dj_hx/guard.py](https://github.com/codetalcott/dj-hx/blob/main/dj_hx/guard.py): the recorded findings
- [dj_hx/middleware.py](https://github.com/codetalcott/dj-hx/blob/main/dj_hx/middleware.py): `HxMiddleware`
- [dj_hx/messages.py](https://github.com/codetalcott/dj-hx/blob/main/dj_hx/messages.py): the messages bridge
- [dj_hx/mixins.py](https://github.com/codetalcott/dj-hx/blob/main/dj_hx/mixins.py): `HxMixin`
- [dj_hx/interactions.py](https://github.com/codetalcott/dj-hx/blob/main/dj_hx/interactions.py): `@interaction`, its registry and the wrapper view
- [dj_hx/urls.py](https://github.com/codetalcott/dj-hx/blob/main/dj_hx/urls.py): the URLconf that serves every interaction
- [dj_hx/templatetags/hx.py](https://github.com/codetalcott/dj-hx/blob/main/dj_hx/templatetags/hx.py): `{% act %}`
- [dj_hx/testing.py](https://github.com/codetalcott/dj-hx/blob/main/dj_hx/testing.py): `HxTestClient`, `assert_no_hx_check_issues`
- [dj_hx/checks.py](https://github.com/codetalcott/dj-hx/blob/main/dj_hx/checks.py): W001 to E026
- [dj_hx/errors.py](https://github.com/codetalcott/dj-hx/blob/main/dj_hx/errors.py): every exception
- [dj_hx/hxlint.py](https://github.com/codetalcott/dj-hx/blob/main/dj_hx/hxlint.py): the htmx 4 lint (vendored from hx-flask)
- [dj_hx/hx_vocab.py](https://github.com/codetalcott/dj-hx/blob/main/dj_hx/hx_vocab.py): the htmx 4.0.2 vocabulary, generated
- [example/](https://github.com/codetalcott/dj-hx/tree/main/example): contact.app on the ORM, the complete reference project
- [tests/](https://github.com/codetalcott/dj-hx/tree/main/tests): one test per row of the failure catalogue
